outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let R=\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]. Suppose that f(x)=x^2-\sqrt{2} factors nontrivially in R[x]. Since f is monic of degree 2 and R is an integral domain, such a factorization would give a linear factor and therefore a root in R. Thus there would exist a,b\in\mathbb{Z} such that
\[
(a+b\sqrt{2})^2=\sqrt{2}.
\]
Expanding gives
\[
a^2+2b^2+2ab\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{2}.
\]
The representation u+v\sqrt{2} with u,v\in\mathbb{Z} is unique, so comparison of the \sqrt{2}-coefficients gives 2ab=1. This is impossible since 2ab is even. Hence f has no root in R and cannot factor nontrivially. Therefore x^2-\sqrt{2} is irreducible over \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}].\end{proof}
